posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
I’m joining the team at @X to lead Product.

I am a huge believer in @SpaceX's mission to extend human consciousness to the stars, so it’s time to make shitposting multiplanetary.

X is the best way to find out what’s happening in the world right now and talk about it. The team has been working tirelessly to make X a better place and product for the people who love it, and many have noticed the recent momentum. My goal is to help accelerate that momentum for our community, new users, and businesses globally by continuing to make this product beautiful and useful.

We are twenty years in, but it truly feels like X’s next chapter will be our greatest. I look forward to your ideas and feedback; I’m sure the replies will be measured and magnanimous.

quote.author: Devon_Eriksen_
quote.name: Devon Eriksen
quote.text:
Humans are a pack animal. 

This may be hard to understand if you are evangelical and think the book of genesis is literal rather than allegorical, but humans are a pack animal. 

What this means is that the human desire for the acceptance and support of a tribe is as fundamental as the desire for food, for air, for water, for sex, for sunlight, for love.

If you tell young men that they cannot have a tribe, they're not going to accept that.

Ever. 

Especially if you tell that only to the young men of one tribe in particular. They're going to wonder why everybody gets to have a tribe and they don't. 

And they're eventually going to decide that you are the enemy. 

Because you are. Anyone who stands between young men and what they need for a healthy, fulfilled life is their enemy. 

That includes you. 

And if you manage to convince them that god doesn't want them to have a tribe, it will also include god. 

The more you push back against their healthy and natural desire for a tribe, a homeland, and a birthright, the more they will hate you, and the more exclusive their definition of that tribe will become. 

There is no way you can stop this. The only thing you can control is how far they have to go, how radical they have to become, in order to get it. 

Because this can go all the way from enforcing immigration law, and shutting down corrupt visa programs right now, to gangs of young White men in balaclavas with Ar15s going door to door ten years from now. 

We have to do something about the 14th amendment. I don't care if that makes you uncomfortable or unhappy. It's not a choice. The constitution exists to serve Americans, not the other way around. If that sentence confuses you, read the first paragraph of the constitution. 

If we do not, young men of the future, the same little boys who are being radicalized right now by your malicious indifference, will treat a piece of paper that says they cannot have a homeland the way they would treat a piece of paper that says that can't eat food, or a piece of paper that says they can't own a home, or have a wife and children. 

You may think that you offer them a tribe in the form of the universal kingdom of god, the community of all believers, but that's just a word game and you know it, which is why you are so defensive about the whole thing. 

Where was the universal community of believers when these young men needed help? When they needed not just the surface appearance of a tribe, but someone to do the things that tribes actually do for younger generations they care about?

The pack serves a concrete set of functions in the life cycle of the human species, and you cannot perform those functions with a cardboard cutout. 

Young men are sick of religion that offers them responsibilities with no rights, lectures with no help, demands with no love or empathy. 

It's odd, in a way ironic, that, I, the man of zero faith, should have to be the one standing here telling self-styled religious leaders how they failed both their people and their god. 

But having no faith does give me one advantage. It frees me from the delusion that Jesus is a puppet that I can pull out of my pocket, slip over my right hand, move his mouth and make him say what I want. 

I used to wonder, as a child, what the phrase "taking the name of the lord in vain" actually meant. 

But I no longer wonder, because when I became a man, I looked around me and saw all these people who talk to god and somehow get told exactly what they want to hear. 

Then I understood that the key phrase here wasn't "in vain". It was "taking". Taking the name of god and using it as a tool for one's own goals. 

Joel, here, is sad that his friend is getting sent home. This personally inconveniences both him and his friend, which effects Joel in a way that young men being denied their birthright does not. 

So he finds an interpretation of scripture that says that god wants him, Joel Berry, to get his way, and that god wants all the young men who want a homeland and a birthright to go get fucked. 

I'm not terribly impressed.

quote.author: Rothmus
quote.name: Rothmus 🏴
quote.text:
Lula packed Brazil’s Supreme Court with his own lawyer and justice minister and had them lock his rival up for 27 years.

Back in 2023, after taking power, he named Cristiano Zanin and Flávio Dino to the court. In 2025 both voted to convict Jair Bolsonaro of a coup plot and hand him the sentence. 
That court had previously wiped Lula’s own corruption convictions in 2021 so he could run again. 

On election day, Zanin ordered the polls kept open another 2 hours, 3 minutes before they were supposed to close. Both sides had asked, but the call came from Lula’s former defense lawyer.

Even after Bolsonaro was barred and jailed, Lula still trailed Flávio 45–47 in the first round and only scraped past him by under 4 points in the runoff. 

Flávio still refuses to concede. Lula called the win a defeat for denialism and lies. 
Two of the judges who put his rival away were the men he put on the court. Voters barely picked him. The court cleared the path.

Not many people know that Elon Musk’s roots go back to the American Midwest. His grandfather, Joshua Haldeman, was born in Minnesota, and his mother, Maye, was born in Canada before the family packed up and moved to South Africa when she was still a little girl. 

Even Elon’s name, which so many people assume is exotic, is a family name. He was named after his great-grandfather, John Elon Haldeman, who around 1900 was a school superintendent and a part-time sheriff in Minnesota. So, yeah, the most futuristic name in the world actually came from a small-town lawman more than a century ago 🤷🏼‍♀️😄

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Michael Dell calls Elon Musk the "most demanding customer there is," and says Musk rewarded Dell with more business after the Colossus build

DELL: “So it shouldn’t be too surprising that we’re also number one in AI infrastructure.”

MIMS: “Dell did half of the servers in the Colossus One AI supercomputer for SpaceX. And you did it really fast, right? I think that was a record fast build. It was like six weeks or something.”

DELL: “Elon is probably the most demanding customer. No, he’s definitely the most demanding customer there is.”

MIMS: “Yeah? Was there a bonus involved? Get this done in six weeks and…”

DELL: “I don’t know that there was a bonus involved, but they have rewarded us with additional business because we’ve done a great job. And that’s pretty much the pattern.”

quote.author: firesidealpha
quote.name: Fireside Alpha
quote.text:
Elon Musk explains how to build AI satellites on the moon from lunar silicon and aluminum, and says 500 to 1,000 terawatts a year cannot be launched from Earth

“Well, the lunar soil is 20% silicon or something like that. So you can mine the silicon on the moon, refine it, and create the solar cells and the radiators on the moon. So get the radiators out of aluminum. So there’s plenty of silicon and aluminum on the moon to make the cells and the radiators. The chips you could send from Earth because they’re pretty light. But maybe at some point you make them on the moon, too."

"Like I said, it does seem like a sort of a video game situation where it’s difficult but not impossible to get to the next level. I don’t see any way that you could do 500 to 1,000 terawatts per year launched from Earth.”
